tasks.spec: Create a Python script named curate_stayin_alive.py in the current task directory. The script must: (1) read the CSV catalog at /home/ankit114/projects/baldev-vimala-photo-sort/catalog/baldev_vimala_photo_manifest.csv (columns include source_path, clip_decade, clip_category, clip_category_score, is_monochrome, width, height). (2) Filter to photos where clip_decade is '1970s' OR '1950s_1960s_or_earlier' (the 70s-and-older era for the Stayin Alive slideshow). (3) Exclude non-people categories: drop any row where clip_category is 'document_or_photo_back', 'album_page_or_collage', or 'unknown'. (4) Sort by clip_category_score descending (highest-confidence classifications first) and pick the top 55 photos. (5) Write the absolute source_path of each selected photo, one per line, to the file at absolute path /tmp/ringer-baldev75/stayin_alive_photos.txt. (6) Also copy each selected photo into a subdirectory at absolute path /tmp/ringer-baldev75/stayin_alive_staging/ preserving just the filename. (7) Print a summary line: SELECTED <N> photos. The script must accept no arguments and read paths from the CSV only. Do not invent or hardcode photo paths - every path must come from the CSV source_path column. Use only the Python standard library (csv, shutil, os, pathlib).
tasks.verified: executing the curation script proves 40-70 real 70s-and-older people photos were selected from the catalog CSV and copied to staging, every path verified on disk

tasks.spec: Create a Python script named curate_full_life.py in the current task directory. The script must: (1) read the CSV catalog at /home/ankit114/projects/baldev-vimala-photo-sort/catalog/baldev_vimala_photo_manifest.csv. (2) Exclude non-people categories: drop rows where clip_category is 'document_or_photo_back', 'album_page_or_collage', or 'unknown'. (3) Group remaining photos by clip_decade. The decades present are: 1950s_1960s_or_earlier, 1970s, 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, 2010s_or_newer. (4) Select photos so EVERY decade is represented, but CAP each decade at 30 photos so 1990s (the largest) cannot dominate. Within each decade, sort by clip_category_score descending and take the top photos up to the cap. Target a total of approximately 120 photos (6 seconds each = ~12 minutes, within the 10-15 min target). (5) Order the final list chronologically by era: 1950s/60s first, then 1970s, 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, 2010s+. (6) Write the absolute source_path of each selected photo, one per line, to the file at absolute path /tmp/ringer-baldev75/full_life_photos.txt. (7) Also copy each selected photo into a subdirectory at absolute path /tmp/ringer-baldev75/full_life_staging/ preserving just the filename. (8) Print SELECTED <N> photos, with per-decade counts. Use only the Python standard library. Do not invent paths - all must come from the CSV.
tasks.verified: executing the curation script proves 100-150 real all-era photos were selected with every decade represented and none over-capped, all paths verified on disk

tasks.spec:
Create a Python script named build_slideshows.py in the current task directory that uses ffmpeg (v7.1.5, on PATH) to build two silent slideshow videos from photo lists. The script must:

(1) Read two input files at absolute paths: /tmp/ringer-baldev75/stayin_alive_photos.txt and /tmp/ringer-baldev75/full_life_photos.txt. Each file has one absolute photo path per line. These files are produced by earlier curation tasks and will already exist in the current directory when this script runs. If either file is missing, print WHY and exit 1.

(2) For EACH photo list, build a video where every photo shows for exactly 6 seconds at 1920x1080 (fit/pad with black background, maintain aspect ratio), with a subtle slow zoom-in (Ken Burns effect) applied via ffmpeg zoompan filter, and a 0.5 second crossfade between consecutive photos. Use a single ffmpeg command per video concatenating all images with the concat demuxer or -loop 1 per image approach.

(3) Apply a WARM 70s aesthetic color grade to the stayin_alive video only: use ffmpeg eq filter to boost warmth (slightly increased red/gamma, reduced blue) and a subtle vignette. Leave full_life video with natural color.

(4) Output two files at absolute paths: /tmp/ringer-baldev75/stayin_alive_slideshow.mp4 and /tmp/ringer-baldev75/full_life_slideshow.mp4. Use libx264, yuv420p pixel format, 30fps, CRF 23. SILENT (no audio track).

(5) The script must invoke ffmpeg as a subprocess and check its return code. If ffmpeg fails on a photo (e.g. unsupported format), skip that photo and continue, logging a warning, rather than failing the whole video. Print BUILD stayin_alive N photos -> stayin_alive_slideshow.mp4 and BUILD full_life N photos -> full_life_slideshow.mp4 as it works.

(6) Accept the photo list absolute paths as arguments: build_slideshows.py /tmp/ringer-baldev75/stayin_alive_photos.txt /tmp/ringer-baldev75/full_life_photos.txt. Use only the Python standard library (subprocess, pathlib, os, sys, json). Do NOT require any pip packages. ffmpeg and ffprobe are invoked as subprocesses.

IMPORTANT: After writing build_slideshows.py, you MUST execute it yourself by running: python3 build_slideshows.py /tmp/ringer-baldev75/stayin_alive_photos.txt /tmp/ringer-baldev75/full_life_photos.txt — and wait for it to finish producing both .mp4 files. The check will only verify the output videos exist and are valid; it will NOT run the build for you. If you only write the script without running it, the check fails.
tasks.verified: executing ffprobe on both output mp4 files proves they are real valid HD videos with durations in the target ranges (stayin ~330s, full ~720s), not fabricated artifacts
